notes.families: From the coarse annotator tags; this is the released scenes.jsonl convention. A scene may be in several.
notes.materials: Resolved leaves, multi-label. They do NOT sum to the family counts: a scene may hold two materials of one family.
notes.material_families: Families implied by the resolved leaves. Differs from `families` on scenes tagged `plastic` whose leaf is `viscoplastic`, a Flowing material.
notes.questions: Yes/No, with the ground-truth answer used to score models. Judge: google/gemini-3.8-flash, 16 frames, one call per scene. Scoring is layer 1 + presence + Missing: a question in a scene with no video, gated, or failing presence counts wrong rather than being skipped.
notes.presence: One presence question per scene, id Q0, category presence. It is a gate, not a score: it asks whether anything in the render could stand in for the scene's main dynamic object, worded so a crude attempt passes. A scene that fails it has all of its other questions counted wrong. It is excluded from n_questions and from the accuracy denominator.

families.label: Rigid and articulated
families.definition: Bodies that hold their shape. Motion is a rigid transform.

families.label: Deformable solid
families.definition: Matter with an elastic stress response that keeps a mesh.

families.label: Co-dimensional
families.definition: Thin structures, where bending rather than stretching carries the motion.

families.label: Flowing
families.definition: Matter with no rest configuration. Correspondence is per particle.

materials.label: Rigid body
materials.definition: Blocks, balls, tools, containers. Six degrees of freedom per body.

materials.label: Articulated body
materials.definition: Rigid links joined by hinges or prismatic joints: arms, grippers, chains.

materials.label: Hyperelastic
materials.definition: Recovers its rest shape: rubber, jelly, springs, soft toys, inflatables.

materials.label: Viscoelastic
materials.definition: Rate-dependent response that relaxes over time: silicone, gels.

materials.label: Elastoplastic
materials.definition: Yields above a stress threshold and keeps the new shape: dough, clay, snow.

materials.label: Shell
materials.definition: Codimension-one surfaces: cloth, paper, foil, film, thin shells.

materials.label: Rod
materials.definition: Codimension-two curves: rope, cable, hair, noodles, slender rods.

materials.label: Granular
materials.definition: Frictional grains flowing as a bulk: sand, rice, beans, cereal, grain.

materials.label: Newtonian fluid
materials.definition: Shear stress proportional to strain rate, no yield stress: water, wine, milk.

materials.label: Viscoplastic fluid
materials.definition: Yield-stress matter that holds shape until loaded, then flows: honey, syrup.

In the first frame, does a flat blue sheet lie on the white table to the right of a silver dumpling press, the two not touching?
In the first frame, is the press open and empty, with the metal bowl and the fluted rim bare?
Does the arm bring its tool down behind the blue sheet and push it to the left across the table onto the press, the sheet bending and folding over the rim as it rides up and staying in one piece?
In the final frame, is the blue sheet draped over the press covering the metal bowl, with only the fluted rim along the near edge and the wire handles still showing?
In the final frame, is the sheet no longer flat, curving over the press with its edge hanging down past the rim?

scenes.description: Robot unfolds aluminium foil
scenes.scene_note: Two robot hands grab a crumpled foil sheet and pull it open into a crinkled sheet.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a crumpled silver foil sheet? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the foil move only where a hand holds it, staying in the stretched shape instead of springing back to crumpled?
In the first frame, does a crumpled silver foil sheet lie flat on the wooden table, with the hand on the right already down on its right edge?
In the first frame, is the hand on the left open and up in the air, not touching anything?
Does the hand on the right close on the foil and lift it off the table, then the hand on the left grip the other side so the two pull apart until the foil opens into a wide sheet?
In the final frame, is the foil pulled open into a wide sheet held up between the two hands, across the middle of the table?
In the final frame, is the sheet covered in creases and wrinkles all over from being crumpled, rather than smooth?

scenes.description: Robot folds a blanket over itself
scenes.scene_note: Two robot hands lift a crumpled plaid blanket's edge and fold it over itself.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a robot hand or a cloth on a table? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the cloth move anywhere the hands are not holding it, or pass through the table or through itself?
In the first frame, does a beige cloth with dark brown checks lie bunched up on the wooden table, heaped up in the middle with deep folds?
In the first frame, are the two white robot hands down at the left and right edge of the cloth, with no part of the cloth lifted off the table?
Do the two hands pinch the near corners and lift the cloth clear of the table, where it sags into a deep U between them, then pull it apart sideways and lower it flat?
In the final frame, is a bunched strip with loose threads still left along the far edge, so the cloth is not smooth?

scenes.description: Robot folds a booklet page over
scenes.scene_note: Two robot hands fold a paper booklet's left page over onto the right page.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a pale pink paper sheet lying flat? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the paper move anywhere no hand is pushing it, or pass through the table or through the other half of the sheet?
In the first frame, does a pale pink paper sheet lie open flat on the wooden table, creased down the middle into two halves?
In the first frame, are both white robot hands up above the table, with neither one touching the paper?

Does the left robot hand push the left half of the sheet up and over the middle crease onto the right half while the right hand stays down at the right edge, the paper bending in a smooth curve without crumpling?
In the final frame, is the sheet folded in half into one narrower rectangle sitting over where the right half was, with the fold edge on the left?
In the final frame, do the two layers at the near edge not lie exactly on top of each other, and are both hands off the paper?

scenes.description: Robot flips a booklet closed
scenes.scene_note: Two robot hands pin and flip one half of a paper booklet to close it.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a white book lying open? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the book move anywhere no hand is touching it, or do the fingers pass through the pages?
In the first frame, is a white book lying open and flat on the wooden table with both pages blank?
In the first frame, are the two robotic hands out to the left and the right of the book, with neither of them touching it?

Does the left hand press flat on the left half while the right hand's fingers slide under the right half and tip it up and over to the left, staying flat and straight as it swings around the spine onto the left half?
In the final frame, is the book closed and lying flat on the table, with the blue printed cover facing up?
In the final frame, are the edges of the closed book straight, with no page bent or sticking out?

scenes.description: Robot whips a rope into a knot
scenes.scene_note: A robot arm whips a hanging rope overhead, flinging it into a tied overhand knot.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a robot arm? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
As the rope swings across the green arm links, does it pass through the arm or through itself where it crosses, rather than staying in front of the links?
In the first frame, does a green robot arm stand on a dark pedestal, bent so the gripper sits at the top, with a white rope held in the gripper?
In the first frame, does the rope hang straight down in front of the pedestal in one smooth line with no bends or loops, with a green tip at its free lower end?

Does the arm straighten up and then whip the gripper over to the left and down, throwing the rope's free end up above the gripper into a big loop that travels down the rope as the end swings back below?
In the final frame, is the arm leaned over to the left with the gripper down on the left side, and the rope hanging from it clear of the pedestal?
In the final frame, is the rope no longer straight, with its lower part curled into a small loop that crosses over itself and the green tip hanging free above the cloth?

scenes.description: Toppling blocks launch a ball off a lever
scenes.scene_note: Growing blocks topple in a chain, slam a lever plank, which launches a ball away.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a row of white dominoes standing upright? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the ball come back down onto the bare floor in front of the fallen dominoes and bounce off to the left out of the frame, without shifting the fallen blocks or passing through them?
In the first frame, is a row of white dominoes standing upright on the wooden floor, getting bigger from left to right, with none tipped over?
In the first frame, is a blue ball at the right end of a wooden plank lying over a small white block, with bare floor between the plank and the biggest domino?
Do the dominoes topple one after the other to the right, the last one dropping onto the left end of the plank and flipping the blue ball up out of the top of the frame?

scenes.description: Three balls race down differently curved tracks
scenes.scene_note: Three balls released together race down curved, straight and arched tracks at different speeds.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a metal rail curving down from a post? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does each ball stay on its own rail all the way down and keep its round shape, without passing through the rails or touching another ball after the start?

In the first frame, do three metal rails run from the top of a post on the left down to a clamp on the right, the top one bulging upwards, the middle one nearly straight and the bottom one dipping steeply then flattening out?

Do the balls get released at the top and roll down one per rail, the orange one on the dipping rail dropping fastest and catching up with the blue one, while the red one on the bulging rail barely drops and stays behind?
In the final frame, are the three balls spread out, each on its own rail, with the orange one lowest and furthest right, the blue one above it and the red one near the top left?
In the final frame, has any of the balls reached the bottom end of the rails?

scenes.description: Marble rolls along a wavy groove
scenes.scene_note: A hand-tipped cup releases a marble that rolls along a wavy groove into a bowl.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a wooden board with a carved wavy groove? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the marble stay inside the groove the whole way, pushed up and down by the wooden waves instead of passing through them?
In the first frame, does a hand hold a blue cup against the right end of the wooden board, with the marble not yet visible?
In the first frame, is the track a wavy groove cut into the board that runs to the left and ends in a round wooden bowl?
Does the blue marble come out of the cup and roll left along the wavy groove, up over each crest and down into each trough, speeding up the further left it gets, and out into the round bowl?
In the final frame, is the blue marble in the round bowl at the left end and still rolling back and forth in it, not yet settled?
In the final frame, is the wavy groove empty, with the hand and the blue cup gone from the right edge?

scenes.description: Cue break triggers a domino chain
scenes.scene_note: Cue strikes ball, triggering a domino chain that tips paddles and knocks balls into pockets.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a cluster of upright white and yellow slats? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does any coloured ball start moving before the tipping slats reach it, or pass through the slats or through another ball?
In the first frame, do six coloured balls sit in a ring around a tight cluster of white and yellow slats standing upright on the green table?
In the first frame, does a row of thin red slats stand upright between the cluster and the white ball on the left, with the cue stick tip behind the white ball cut off by the left edge?
Does the white ball roll right and stop against the left end of the red slats, after which the slats tip over outward from the centre and shove the six coloured balls away in six directions?
In the final frame, are all six coloured balls gone off the table, with only the white ball left sitting against the left end of the red slats?
In the final frame, have all the slats tipped over flat, the red ones into one long ribbed band and the white and yellow ones into six arrows pointing out from the centre?

scenes.description: Wine pours and sloshes into a glass
scenes.scene_note: A red wine stream pours into a glass, churning and sloshing up the wall.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a tilted wine glass with dark red wine? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
At any point, does any wine splash over the rim or pass through the glass wall instead of staying inside the glass?
In the first frame, is a wine glass tilted to the right with dark red wine in the bottom of the bowl, its stem and base cut off by the bottom edge?
In the first frame, does a red wine stream pour in from the top edge over the left side of the rim as one connected wobbly ribbon, with no bottle visible?
Does the stream fall into the left half of the glass and plunge under the surface, with the wine collecting on the low right side of the tilted bowl as the level climbs?
In the final frame, is the pour still going with the wine level risen, the dark wine sitting higher up the right wall of the bowl?
In the final frame, is the wine surface churned up with a pale pink froth patch on it where the stream goes in?

scenes.description: Rocking tank sends breaking waves
scenes.scene_note: A driven pivoting tank rocks back and forth, sending breaking water waves along it.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a clear tank of blue water? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
At any point, does the water move without the tank tilting, or pass through the clear walls?
In the first frame, is a long clear tank with blue water in it tilted down to the right on a white mount on a grey board?
In the first frame, does the water lie along the whole bottom and sit deeper at the low right end, with a choppy surface carrying small crests?
Does the tank rock on the mount down to the left and then back down to the right while the water sloshes end to end and runs up the raised end as a wave?
In the final frame, is the tank tilted down to the right again but with the water heaped up at the raised left end?
In the final frame, does the water surface slope down from the left heap to a thin layer at the low right end instead of lying level?

scenes.description: Domino pyramid collapses into a pile
scenes.scene_note: A domino track topples into a domino pyramid, which collapses into a spread pile.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a pyramid of upright coloured dominoes? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
At any point, does a domino tip before the one before it hits it, or do fallen dominos pass through each other?
In the first frame, is a nine-level pyramid built from upright pink, teal and grey dominos with flat yellow and grey dominos laid across them as bridges?
In the first frame, do the dominos in front of the pyramid stand in rows that run off both the left and right edges, all upright and none tipped?
Does the tipping start at the bottom left corner of the frame and run along the rows in front of the pyramid, after which the pyramid topples from left to right?
In the final frame, is the pyramid gone and lying flat in a heap on the ground, with every domino still a whole rigid block, none bent or broken?
In the final frame, is any domino left standing anywhere in the frame, including in the rows that run out to both edges?

scenes.description: Swing seat oscillates on chains
scenes.scene_note: Rigid swing seat on chains oscillates back and forth as a pendulum.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a yellow swing seat hanging on chains? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
At any point, does the seat touch the blue post as it crosses in front of it, or touch the ground?
In the first frame, does a yellow plastic baby swing seat hang on four chains just left of the blue post, well above the red ground?
In the first frame, do the chains run up out of the top of the frame, with the bar they hang from not visible?
Does the yellow seat swing left and right across the frame for about four full passes, hanging lowest crossing the middle, riding up at both ends and reaching less far each pass?
In the final frame, has the yellow seat swung over to the right side of the frame, hanging in front of the blue post?
In the final frame, is the seat the same shape as at the start, with the hard plastic not bent or dented and the chains still straight?

scenes.description: Magnetic ball strands zip together
scenes.scene_note: Two hand-held magnetic ball strands zip together ball by ball into a double row.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like two strands of silver metal balls? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
As the two rows pull together, do any balls stop touching along their strand, or overlap or pass through each other?
In the first frame, do two strands of silver metal balls run in from the left edge to a hand on the right, forming a wide open v with white table between them?
In the first frame, is each strand a single row of same sized balls touching end to end, with the left ends of both strands cut off by the frame edge?
Do the two strands snap together starting at the hand, with the closing point travelling left along them until it runs off the left edge of the frame?
In the final frame, have the two strands closed together into one straight flat band running from the hand off the left edge, with the v gone?
In the final frame, do the balls of the two rows sit offset, each ball in the dip between two balls of the other row with no gap left between the strands?

scenes.description: Marble knocks a pivoting lever aside
scenes.scene_note: Marble rolls down ramps and knocks a pivoting taped lever board aside.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a dark wood board with light wooden rails? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
At any point on the way down, does the marble sink into a rail or pass through one instead of riding on top of it?
In the first frame, are light wooden rails taped onto a dark wood board at different angles with gaps between them, the long rail with the blue tape lying almost flat across the middle?
In the first frame, is the silver marble in the frame?

Does the silver marble roll right along the top rail and drop off its end onto the long taped rail, which tips over under it and swings up past upright, the marble then zig zagging down the lower rails and off the right edge?
In the final frame, is the long taped rail standing up steeply, with its lower end down on the bottom rail?
In the final frame, is the marble still seen?

scenes.description: Conveyor carries foam cubes along guides
scenes.scene_note: A moving belt carries foam cubes that slide and turn along angled guides.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a black conveyor belt with two yellow rails? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Do the cubes move only because the belt carries them, with the yellow rails staying in the same place and no cube penetrating a rail or another cube?
In the first frame, do the two yellow rails sit over the belt at an angle, with neither end of the belt in the frame?
In the final frame, is the blue cube past the left yellow rail and further out on the belt, with the green cube that started at that rail gone out of the frame on the left?
In the final frame, have the red and the green cube come down to the left rail, with all the cubes still having sharp corners and none of them tipped over?

scenes.description: Dominoes topple along an S-shaped track
scenes.scene_note: Rigid dominoes along an S-shaped track topple in a chain, dropping elevated tops.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a curving line of coloured dominoes? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does each domino move only when the one behind it hits it, with the fallen ones stacking on each other without passing through each other or into the ground?
In the first frame, do pink, teal and yellow dominoes stand on the concrete in a line curving into a big S, with straight lines running off the left edge and the top right?
In the final frame, is the whole S knocked down except for two pink dominoes still standing at the corner where the top of the S meets the line going off to the right?
In the final frame, are the fallen dominoes still sharp edged blocks, none bent or broken, with those in the straight line at the left lying stacked leaning on each other?

scenes.description: Domino lines flip blocks down stair lanes
scenes.scene_note: Domino lines trigger blocks that flip down stair lanes, knocking a panel onto more dominoes.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a line of white dominoes on stairs? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Do the cards pass through the yellow blocks on the steps, or do any of those blocks move as the cards flip over them?
In the first frame, is a blue card standing upright on the top step of the teal stairs and a red card on the top step of the pink stairs?
In the first frame, is the line of white dominoes running up to the top of the stairs all standing upright, with none of them tipped?
Does the white domino line topple along until it reaches the top of the stairs and knocks both cards over?
Does each card tumble end over end down its own staircase, staying stiff with sharp corners instead of bending?
In the final frame, is the white domino line at the top left all down, leaning on each other in a sawtooth?

scenes.description: Tyre flattens gel toys and one splits
scenes.scene_note: Car tire rolls over gel squishies, flattening them; they spring back, one splits open.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a row of round squishy toys? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
In the first frame, do three round squishy toys, a pink one, an orange one and a yellow one, sit side by side on the asphalt, all three plump and undeformed?
In the first frame, is the black tire at the right edge of the frame next to the yellow toy, with only a small clump of pink beads on the ground under the orange one?
Does the tire roll to the left over the row and squash the yellow toy first, then the orange and then the pink, each flattening into a wide low blob under the tread?

scenes.description: Domino chain topples floor loops
scenes.scene_note: A stick starts a domino chain that slides down a track and topples floor loops.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a looping line of coloured dominoes? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does each domino fall only when the one before it hits it, without passing through each other or through the black rail, while the rail on its blue stand stays in the same place from start to end?
In the first frame, do the coloured dominoes all stand upright in a long line that winds in loops over the wooden floor and runs off the right edge, its end not visible?
In the first frame, does a white domino stand at the top end of the black rail, with the slots down the rest of the rail filled with upright coloured dominoes?
Does a wooden stick come in from the left and tip the white domino at the top of the rail, with the toppling running down the rail and then on along the line on the floor?
In the final frame, is every domino knocked down with not one left standing, lying flat and overlapping each other along the same curved path the line had?
In the final frame, are the slots of the black rail all empty, with the dominoes that stood in it slid down to its low end and the white one among them?

scenes.description: Mousetrap snaps shut on a smaller trap
scenes.scene_note: Dropped small trap trips a larger mousetrap whose spring bar snaps over onto it.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a mousetrap? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
As the tilted trap snaps, does a long thin wire swing up off it and end up pointing up and to the right, above the traps?
Does the snap of the tilted trap also set off the flat mousetrap resting under it, so that both traps end up closed?

In the first frame, are there two wooden Victor mousetraps on a dark textured floor in front of a brick wall, one lying flat with a pink bait pedal and a second propped at an angle behind it with a yellow bait pedal?
In the first frame, are both mousetraps still set, with each snap bar held back towards the right and neither one closed?
Does the tilted mousetrap with the yellow pedal snap shut, its bar swinging over the pedal, while the flat mousetrap with the pink pedal stays set?
In the final frame, is the yellow-pedal trap closed and lying flatter and further left than where it started, with the pink-pedal trap still set and its bar held back?

scenes.description: Milk pours onto cornflakes
scenes.scene_note: A milk stream pours onto cornflakes, splashing droplets and pooling between the flakes.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a white bowl of yellow cornflakes? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Do the flakes move only where the milk reaches them, without sinking through the bowl or through each other?
In the first frame, is a white bowl full of yellow curled cornflakes with a white milk stream falling into its middle?
In the first frame, does the milk stream come in from the top edge of the frame, with whatever pours it not visible?
Does the milk come down as one unbroken rope that breaks into splashes and droplets only where it lands on the flakes, while the stream drifts left across the bowl?
In the final frame, are the flakes where the stream lands pushed down with milk pooled between them, the flakes still whole and yellow?
In the final frame, are white milk droplets scattered in the black background above and to the right of the bowl?

scenes.description: Water spills over a brim-full bucket
scenes.scene_note: A water stream pours into a brim-full bucket, churning the surface and spilling over.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a blue bucket full of water? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does any water pass through the bucket wall instead of leaving over the rim and running down the outside?
In the first frame, is a blue bucket filled to the rim with a water stream falling in from the top edge, the bucket bottom and ground not visible?
In the first frame, is water running over the left side of the rim and down the outside wall?
Does the stream pour the whole clip as a clear column that breaks into white froth where it hits the surface, with the extra water leaving over the left rim?
In the final frame, is the bucket still full to the rim with water spilling over the left side, the level not risen above the rim?
In the final frame, is the surface churned into white foam and bubbles around where the stream lands, rather than flat?

scenes.description: Press flattens a rubber ball into a disc
scenes.scene_note: A hydraulic press plate descends and flattens a rubber ball into a thin disc.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a rainbow ball on a round steel plate? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the ball flatten only while the top plate pushes down, with the rubber squeezed sideways past the plate edge and not passing through either plate?
In the first frame, is a rainbow ball, pink to orange to yellow to green, sitting round and unsquashed on a round steel plate?
In the first frame, is the round steel top plate right above the ball and wider than the ball?
In the final frame, is the ball shape gone, the rubber pressed into a thin flat band pinched between the two plates and sticking out past their rim?
In the final frame, is the squeezed rubber wrinkled into folds at the pink end and still one piece, with nothing broken off onto the table?

scenes.description: Domino wave collapses a grid of sticks
scenes.scene_note: Domino chain wave topples supports, collapsing a grid of sticks onto the floor.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like upright dominoes standing in rows? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
In the first frame, do black dominos stand upright in a grid with wooden sticks laid across them in two levels, nothing leaning or fallen?
In the first frame, does a long line of coloured dominos stand upright in front of the grid, running in from the left edge so the first one is not visible?
Does the coloured line topple along its length into the black legs at the front left, after which the grid comes down and the collapse spreads right and back?

scenes.description: Marbles spiral through a zigzag feeder
scenes.scene_note: Many marbles roll through a zigzag feeder and spiral lanes, dropping through the center hole.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a white spiral ramp with coloured marbles? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
As the marbles knock into each other, do any of them lose their hard round shape or pass through each other or the walls of the spiral?
In the first frame, is the white spiral ramp full of red, yellow, green and blue marbles lying in its grooves, with a dark round hole in the middle?
Do the marbles roll down the zigzag track onto the outer ring of the spiral, round the grooves inwards, and drop out one by one through the middle hole?
In the final frame, are exactly 10 marbles left in the spiral grooves, with one blue marble sitting down in the hole in the middle?

scenes.description: Melted chocolate coils into a mould
scenes.scene_note: Thick melted chocolate pours as a rope from a bowl, coiling into a spreading pool in a mold.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a light brown triangle chocolate mould? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the chocolate run over the divider into the neighbouring compartments or pass through the mould?
In the first frame, is a light brown chocolate mould with triangle pyramid compartments sitting on the dark speckled counter?
In the first frame, is thick chocolate already pouring into the right compartment from a clear jug cut off by the right edge, with the triangle tips still sticking out above the chocolate?

Does the thick chocolate pour into the right compartment the whole clip, the falling rope coiling and folding over itself where it lands while the pool builds up and spreads over the triangle pattern, without splashing or breaking into drops?
In the final frame, is the stream still pouring, with the chocolate stacked up in fine folds around where it lands?

scenes.description: Ram compresses a coil spring shut
scenes.scene_note: A hydraulic ram descends and compresses a coil spring until its coils close.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a coil spring on a striped block? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Does the spring shorten only while the press head pushes down on it, the coils pressing onto each other without passing through each other or the lower block?
In the first frame, does a dark grey coil spring stand upright on the flat top of the lower yellow and black striped block, with open gaps between all its coils?
In the first frame, is the striped press head above the spring already touching the top coil, with no gap under its bottom face?
Does the press head move straight down and shorten the spring, the gaps closing from the top coil downwards until all coils touch, then stop and stay there?
In the final frame, has the press head come down and squashed the spring to under half its starting height, with the coils stacked flat and no gaps left?
In the final frame, are the coils still round and the spring standing on the same spot of the lower block, not bent over to one side?

scenes.description: Tennis balls bounce off racket strings
scenes.scene_note: Tennis balls bounce onto the court and a racket's strings, rolling apart to rest.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a black racket with a yellow grip? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Do the balls sink through the strings or the court, or does the racket move when a ball lands on it?
In the first frame, does a black racket with a yellow grip lie on the blue green court with empty strings?
In the first frame, are two tennis balls cut off by the right edge of the frame, with the rest of the court empty?
Do balls keep coming in from the right edge and bounce leftwards across the court and off the racket strings, with lower hops each time until they only roll?
In the final frame, are 4 balls in the frame, one resting on the strings at the left edge of the racket head, one on the court in front of the racket and two cut off by the top edge?
In the final frame, is any of the balls flattened or dented where it landed?

scenes.description: Press crushes a duck on rubber rings
scenes.scene_note: A press ram crushes a rubber duck atop a stack of rubber rings, which squash and slide.

questions.question: In the first frame, is there something that looks like a yellow duck on a stack of rings? Answer Yes even if it is crude, roughly shaped, or a different colour.
Do the rings squash and bulge out sideways where the press pushes, without passing through each other or through the press head?
In the first frame, does a stack of 5 plastic rings sit on the striped press bed, orange, yellow, blue, pink, green from the bottom, with a yellow duck on top?
Does the press head move down onto the duck and flatten it out to the left, then the rings squash down and tilt over sideways?
In the final frame, has the press head come far down with the stack squashed flat, and are the green and the pink ring no longer visible?
In the final frame, is the bottom orange ring pressed out wide and bulging sideways past the rest, with the duck squeezed out flat to the left?
